No host or FPGA deployment, no new hardware test and no throughput improvement claimed.
ACK counts cover data words on every sixty-fourth successful read, excluding the command-byte handshake. Deterministic sampling can miss waits on unsampled chunks.
ACK counts are not durations and do not independently distinguish normal round-trip latency from FIFO-full backpressure. They must be interpreted with read/transfer times and the known protocol.

Clock calls and longer log records add observer overhead. The sampled path adds counters but no register reads, writes, per-word clocks or per-word logging. Hardware noninterference remains to be checked.

Poll elapsed time excludes the final profile-log write and diagnostic close; entry-to-entry intervals include other main-loop work. These are service-interval observations, not direct user-interface response latency.
Harnesses mock clocks, pipes and register responses; they verify software traces and accounting, not physical bridge timing, throughput, or a full MiSTer replay.
